snippet.title: 20 Eggs = 20 Chances? Not Quite.
snippet.description:
If you freeze 20 eggs, you don't get 20 chances at a baby. Think of it as a talent show: the thaw, fertilization, growing to a day-5 embryo, and a chromosome round that gets tougher with age. At one large egg-freezing clinic, about 2–3 out of 10 thawed eggs from women who froze before 38 became a chromosomally normal embryo; at 38 or later, less than 1 out of 10.

Full video: https://youtu.be/J21RLRUE1g8

Source: Klein et al., Fertility and Sterility 2025 — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2025.12.003

English voice generated with AI from Dr Aksoy's own voice; lip movements adjusted with AI. Educational only, not personal medical advice.
